facts.statement: The first specimen of Yaverlandia was described in 1930 by D. M. S. Watson.
facts.quote: When the first known specimen, MIWG 1530, was first described in 1930 by D. M. S. Watson

facts.statement: Peter Galton recognized Yaverlandia as a distinct genus in 1971 after re-examining the remains.
facts.quote: It was recognised as a distinct genus in 1971 by Peter Galton, who re-examined the remains.

facts.statement: The holotype was discovered in 1923 by F. M. G. Abell on the Isle of Wight.
facts.quote: It was discovered in 1923 by F. M. G. Abell in the Wealden Marls north of the seawall below Yaverland Battery of Sandown, on the Isle of Wight.

facts.statement: Peter Galton created a cast of the specimen in 1971 to aid his examination.
facts.quote: In 1971, Peter Galton re-examined the specimen, creating a cast for examination.

facts.statement: A second specimen of Yaverlandia was discovered in 2012 by a student during a school fossil hunt.
facts.quote: In 2012, a second specimen referable to Yaverlandia was discovered by a student on a school fossil-hunting trip in Yaverland on the Isle of Wight.

facts.statement: Naish and Steven C. Sweetman described the second specimen in 2026.
facts.quote: Naish and Steven C. Sweetman described this specimen in 2026.

facts.statement: Yaverlandia is an extinct genus found in Lower Cretaceous strata of the Wessex Formation on the Isle of Wight, England.
facts.quote: Yaverlandia (meaning "of Yaverland Point/Yaverland Battery") is an extinct genus of possible dinosaur known from two partial fossil skulls found in Lower Cretaceous strata of the Wessex Formation (Upper Silty Bed) in the Isle of Wight, England.

facts.statement: The fossils date to the Hauterivian and Barremian ages of the Wealden Group.
facts.quote: It originated from strata belonging to the Wealden Group, presumably the Wessex Formation, which on the Isle of Wight dates to the Hauterivian and Barremian ages.

facts.statement: Peter Galton believed Yaverlandia was the oldest member of the family Pachycephalosauridae.
facts.quote: He believed that it was the oldest member of the family Pachycephalosauridae.

facts.statement: Darren Naish suggested in 2008 that Yaverlandia may be related to maniraptoran theropods.
facts.quote: Subsequent research by Darren Naish in 2008 instead suggested affinities with maniraptoran theropods.

facts.statement: Recent research suggests Yaverlandia's identity is enigmatic, with features comparable to both dinosaurs and non-dinosaurian reptiles like crocodyliforms.
facts.quote: These researchers determined that the identity of Yavelandia remains enigmatic; while dinosaur affinities remain possible, some anatomical features are comparable to non-dinosaurian reptiles such as crocodyliforms.

facts.statement: Darren Naish later suggested Yaverlandia was a maniraptoran theropod rather than a pachycephalosaurid.
facts.quote: Naish later suggested that Yaverlandia was not a pachycephalosaurid, as initially suggested, but rather may have been a theropod, and more specifically a maniraptoran.

facts.statement: In 2011, Naish suggested Yaverlandia was a troodontid, but his redescription has not yet been published.
facts.quote: In 2011, Naish suggested that it was a troodontid, and prepared a redescription of the genus, but this has yet to be published.

facts.statement: Researchers noted that no anatomical features definitively support placing Yaverlandia in any specific clade, including maniraptoran theropods or pachycephalosaurs.
facts.quote: They noted that no anatomical features could be recognized that definitively supported a placement of Yavelandia with any specific clade, including maniraptoran theropods and pachycephalosaurs.

facts.statement: Naish and Sweetman concluded that the phylogenetic affinities of Yaverlandia remain unclear.
facts.quote: Naish & Sweetman concluded that the phylogenetic affinities of Yaverlandia remained unclear.

facts.statement: The scientific name of the species is Yaverlandia bitholus.
facts.quote: Galton gave it the binomial name of Yaverlandia bitholus.

facts.statement: Yaverlandia is characterized by two small domes, a pitted dorsal surface, and specific features of the frontal and supratemporal fenestra.
facts.quote: Galton diagnosed Yaverlandia based on the presence of two small domes (one per frontal), a dorsal (upper) surface covered in small pits, a frontal which contributed to the edge of the orbit (eye socket) and was not excluded from it by the prefrontal bone, and a supratemporal fenestra which was not constricted by the postorbital bone, nor reduced as in late pachycephalosaurid genera.

facts.statement: Yaverlandia is classified within the superorder Dinosauria.
facts.quote: superordo: Dinosauria

facts.statement: Yaverlandia is tentatively classified within the unranked family Maniraptora.
facts.quote: unranked_familia: ¿Maniraptora ?

facts.statement: The environment where Yaverlandia lived experienced frequent wildfires that stifled dense plant growth.
facts.quote: Burned plant and insect material and fusain suggest that the environment experienced frequent wildfires, stifling much of the dense growth of gymnosperms.

facts.statement: Most vertebrate fossils from the Wessex Formation, including Yaverlandia, come from plant debris beds caused by flooding.
facts.quote: Most vertebrate material from the Wessex Formation originates from plant debris beds, resulting from the aforementioned flooding events.

facts.statement: Yaverlandia is the only known species in the extinct genus Yaverlandia.
facts.quote: Yaverlandia bitholus es la única especie conocida del género extinto Yaverlandia

facts.statement: Yaverlandia measured approximately 1 meter in length and 30 centimeters in height.
facts.quote: Yaverlandia medía aproximadamente 1 metro de largo y30 centímetros de altura

facts.statement: Only a thick skull with two marked bumps on the dome is known from Yaverlandia.
facts.quote: De él se conoce sólo un cráneo grueso, con dos protuberancias marcadas en el domo

facts.statement: The holotype skull, MIWG 1530, was discovered in England in 1930.
facts.quote: MIWG 1530, el cráneo holotipo, fue descubierto en 1930 en Inglaterra

facts.statement: The holotype skull was commented on by Watson in 1930.
facts.quote: MIWG 1530, el cráneo holotipo, fue descubierto en 1930 en Inglaterra y fue comentado por Watson en 1930

facts.statement: Yaverlandia was originally described as a basal pachycephalosaurid, but Darren Naish later demonstrated it is a theropod, apparently a maniraptor.
facts.quote: Fue descrito en un primer momento como miembro basal de los paquicefalosáuridos, pero recientemente en un trabajo de Darren Naish se demostró que se trata de un terópodo, aparentemente un maniraptor

facts.statement: Peter Malcolm Galton named the fossil Yaverlandia in 1971 and described it as a pachycephalosaurid.
facts.quote: Peter Malcolm Galton en 1971 nombró el fósil como Yaverlandia, al que describió como un paquicefalosáurido

facts.statement: Sullivan, Sereno, and Naish reclassified Yaverlandia as a maniraptoran in works ranging from 2000 to 2008.
facts.quote: Sullivan en 2000, Sereno en ese mismo año y Naish en su tesis no publicada de 2006, Sullivan de 2006 y Naish en 2008 reclasificaron a Yaverlandia como maniraptorano

facts.statement: Yaverlandia lived approximately 125 million years ago during the Barremian stage of the early Cretaceous in what is now Europe.
facts.quote: que vivió principios del período Cretácico, hace aproximadamente 125 millones de años, en el Barremiense, en lo que es hoy Europa

facts.statement: The time range for Yaverlandia is from the Hauterivian to the Barremian, between 132.6 and 121.4 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Hauterivian to Barremian (132.6 to 121.4 million years ago)

facts.statement: Yaverlandia fossils were originally reported from the Wessex Formation of the Isle of Wight but are now identified from the underlying Vectis Formation.
facts.quote: El terreno en el que se encontraron los restos fue en un principio informado como de la Formación Wessex de la Isla de Wight, aunque posteriores trabajos lo identifican de los lechos limosos de la subyacente Formación Vectis

facts.statement: Yaverlandia belongs to the parent group Theropoda.
facts.quote: Parent group: Theropoda

facts.statement: Yaverlandia is classified in the class Reptilia.
facts.quote: Class: Reptilia

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Yaverlandia is Yaverlandia bitholus.
facts.quote: Type species: Yaverlandia bitholus

facts.statement: Additional remains were reported in 2012, but they have not yet been described.
facts.quote: En 2012 se reportaron restos adicionales, pero estos no han sido descritos
